correctness.rationale: Conditional finite-event transform is an exact product of rational Mittag–Leffler Laplace factors. Harmonic expansion is uniform in binomial counts, and concentration proves the stable exponent classification. Subordination by exponential maxima and the exact stable-ratio mean establish alpha-invariance for every finite n. A Taylor expansion with bounded second moments of centered exponential maxima proves the universal logarithmic correction with O(log^-2 n) error; Stieltjes inversion recovers the classical density. Exact rational checks and density quadrature agree.

value.rationale: The expected fraction is exactly insensitive to the fractional index at every n despite infinite raw waiting-time means, a structural fact relevant to identifiability and inferential observability. The leading occupation law discards Bernoulli bias, its first correction reveals precisely the log odds at 1/log n, and polynomial thinning yields a meaningful stable-ratio transition. These are natural consequences of the motivating model, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
